## Problem 1. d)

```{r}
set.seed(123)

# Parameters
alpha <- 1
beta <- 1
L <- 20
N <- 1000

# Function to simulate one delivery time
simulate_delivery <- function(alpha, beta, L) {
  i <- 0
  t <- 0
  while (i < L) {
    if (i == 0) {
      # Reflecting boundary: can only move forward
      rate <- alpha
      t <- t + rexp(1, rate)
      i <- i + 1
    } else {
      # Interior: move forward or backward
      rate <- alpha + beta
      t <- t + rexp(1, rate)
      if (runif(1) < alpha / (alpha + beta)) {
        i <- i + 1
      } else {
        i <- i - 1
      }
    }
  }
  return(t)
}

# Run N simulations
times <- replicate(N, simulate_delivery(alpha, beta, L))

# Results
cat("Simulated mean m0:  ", mean(times), "\n")
cat("Theoretical m0:     ", L*(L+1)/(2*alpha), "\n")
cat("Simulated variance: ", var(times), "\n")
```

# Problem 4 Plot

```{r}
# Parameters
beta <- 1
m_vals <- 1:50

# Stochastic: E[tau_m] = H_{m-1} / beta
H <- cumsum(1/(1:(max(m_vals)-1)))
stochastic <- c(0, H) / beta

# Deterministic: log(m) / beta
deterministic <- log(m_vals) / beta

# Plot
plot(m_vals, stochastic, type = "l", col = "blue", lwd = 2,
     xlab = "m (number of particles)",
     ylab = "Time",
     main = "Yule Process: Stochastic vs Deterministic arrival time")
lines(m_vals, deterministic, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("bottomright", legend = c("Stochastic: H_{m-1}/beta", "Deterministic: log(m)/beta"),
       col = c("blue", "red"), lwd = 2, lty = c(1, 2))
```
